fields.description:
Keep a re-run's pull request diff to the ticket's change when the base branch moved after an earlier execution published to the same agent branch.

`commit_and_push` in `adapters/real/git_host.py` publishes the workspace's verified tree with `git commit-tree <tree> -p <remote head>` whenever the agent branch already exists on the remote. `adapters/real/local_git_host.py` does the same against the local branch head. Parenting on the branch head is what lets the repair loop stack commits within one execution, because the workspace moves forward only by the commits the platform publishes.

A later execution resets its workspace to the current base. When the base has moved since the earlier execution published, the branch head still sits on the old base. The new commit then carries the new base's tree on top of the old history, so the base is not an ancestor of the branch and `git diff base...branch` reports every file that changed on the base in between. Execution `intake-1ea674f2` for rebar ticket `ff34-7786-fef6-4252` on `archive-massgov-pfml` published commit `e80a276` with parent `6b2f996` (on base `aa113d9`) and the tree of base `9ea775e` plus four ticket files. The commit changes 1003 files against its parent, and a pull request opened from the branch would have shown all of them.

When the workspace's commit is not an ancestor of the branch head, publish a commit whose parents are the branch head and the workspace's commit. The branch keeps its earlier history, the push stays a fast-forward, and the base becomes an ancestor of the branch, so the merge-base diff that GitHub and the local backend's patch use covers only the ticket's files. When the workspace's commit is already an ancestor of the branch head, the single-parent behaviour stays unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A publish after the base moved leaves the base an ancestor of the branch and limits the merge-base diff to the change, proven by `pytest tests/integration/test_github_real_backend.py -k publish_after_the_base_moved_keeps_the_merge_base_diff_to_the_change`
- [ ] The same publish is a fast-forward of the earlier branch head, proven by `pytest tests/integration/test_github_real_backend.py -k publish_after_the_base_moved_fast_forwards_the_branch`
- [ ] The local backend's patch after the base moved lists only the change, proven by `pytest tests/unit/test_local_git_host.py -k publish_after_the_base_moved_keeps_the_patch_to_the_change`
- [ ] A repair publish within one execution keeps a single parent, proven by `pytest tests/integration/test_github_real_backend.py -k repair_publish_within_an_execution_keeps_a_single_parent`
- [ ] A re-run on an unchanged base keeps a single parent, proven by `pytest tests/integration/test_github_real_backend.py -k rerun_on_an_unchanged_base_keeps_a_single_parent`
- [ ] A local re-run on an unchanged base keeps a single parent, proven by `pytest tests/unit/test_local_git_host.py -k rerun_on_an_unchanged_base_keeps_a_single_parent`

## Testing
Run each acceptance criterion selector on its own with `python -m pytest`, which imports the checkout under test rather than the editable install. Run `PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" .venv/bin/inv ci` before closing the ticket.
